questions: Does the movement continue while you are asleep?
Can you stop the movement by trying to control it?
Is the movement present when your hand is completely at rest and supported?
Is this the first time you have had this movement?
Do you have any weakness in that hand or arm?
Have you noticed any stiffness or slowness in your movements?
Do you have any numbness or tingling in that hand?
Did you have any warning feeling before it started?
Has anyone in your family had a similar problem?
orders: Observe the patient holding both arms outstretched in front of them
Finger-to-nose testing in the affected hand
Test rapid alternating movements in both hands to assess for dysdiadochokinesia
Examine the contralateral hand for postural tremor
Assess for head, voice, or chin tremor
Check for improvement of tremor after a small amount of alcohol

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Acute right middle cerebral artery territory ischaemic stroke presenting as epilepsia partialis continua (focal motor status epilepticus)

Alternatives:
MELAS syndrome (mitochondrial encephalopathy, lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes)
Herpes simplex encephalitis with secondary ischaemia
Recurrent cardioembolic stroke (e.g. PFO, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation)
